title: Prime In Diagonal
statement:
`nums` is a square grid of integers with `n` rows and `n` columns. A value counts as being on a diagonal when it sits at some position `nums[i][i]` (the main diagonal) or `nums[i][n - 1 - i]` (the anti-diagonal).

Return the biggest prime among the values on either diagonal, or `0` if neither diagonal holds a prime. A prime is an integer greater than `1` whose only positive divisors are `1` and itself.
notes:
## Intuition

Only the two diagonals matter, which is at most `2n` cells, so the work is in testing each value for primality. Values reach `4 · 10^6`, so trial division by every candidate divisor up to the square root (at most about 2,000 checks) is fast. A sieve up to the largest diagonal value would also work but needs megabytes of memory for one small question.

## Approach

1. Write `isPrime(value)`: values below 2 are not prime; otherwise try every `divisor` with `divisor * divisor <= value`.
2. Keep `best = 0`.
3. For each row `i`, look at `nums[i][i]` and `nums[i][n - 1 - i]`.
4. If a value is larger than `best` and prime, it becomes the new `best`.
5. Return `best` (still `0` when no diagonal value was prime).

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 3`. Row 0 gives `1` (not prime) and `3` (prime, `best = 3`). Row 1 gives `6` twice (the centre is on both diagonals), not prime. Row 2 gives `11` (prime and larger, `best = 11`) and `9` (smaller, skipped without a primality test). The answer is `11`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · √V), where V is the largest value: 2n values, each tested in O(√V).
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- `1` is not prime; return `0`, not `1`, when nothing qualifies.
- Loop while `divisor * divisor <= value` (with `<=`), or squares of primes such as `3996001 = 1999²` slip through as primes.
- Check only the two diagonals; a large prime elsewhere in the grid does not count.
- Checking `value > best` first skips needless primality tests.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `isPrime` | trial-division primality test |
| `divisor` | candidate divisor inside `isPrime` |
| `n` | side length of the grid |
| `best` | largest prime seen on a diagonal so far |
| `i` | row index; its diagonal cells are columns `i` and `n - 1 - i` |
| `value` | the diagonal value being examined |
